Talk me through how you review and scrub an AEA Concur expense report once it’s ready.
First the reviewer adds the report to the Excel review tracker.
What does the reviewer record in the Excel review tracker?
Cardholder, statement total, submitted amount, report identifier, and status.
What does the reviewer check in the expense report itself?
Receipts and personal-expense classification on each line, then the approvals.
What determines whether a receipt is adequate and a line is correctly classified as personal?
The current AEA rulebook; the receipt threshold is not confirmed yet.
What does the reviewer check in the report’s approvals?
Approvers and statuses in Concur, then screenshots them and saves the report PDF.
What does the reviewer do when a receipt or personal-expense check does not meet the AEA rulebook?
Flags it to the submitter or client and records the resolution in the tracker.
When an issue is flagged to the submitter or client, what happens to the report while its resolution is pending?
It stays out of the scrubbing batch; only cleared reports go in.

memo_findings.answer: Expense Processing: T&E Review & Scrubbing (AEA Variant)
Work starts when AEA Concur expense reports become ready for review.

Once an AEA Concur expense report is ready for review, the reviewer adds the report to the Excel review tracker.
When a ready AEA Concur expense report is added to the Excel review tracker, the reviewer records the cardholder, statement total, submitted amount, report identifier, and status.
The reviewer checks receipts and personal-expense classification on each report line, then checks approvals.
After the line checks, the reviewer checks approvers and statuses in Concur, screenshots them and saves the report PDF.
When a receipt or personal-expense check does not meet the AEA rulebook, the reviewer flags it to the submitter or client and records the resolution in the tracker.
A report with a flagged issue stays out of the scrubbing batch while resolution is pending; only cleared reports go into the batch.
How a flagged issue is resolved and who clears the report for the batch have not been described.

The reviewer checks receipts and the personal-expense classification on each line of the expense report, then checks the approvals.
The receipt threshold, detailed receipt and personal-expense criteria, and approval acceptance criteria remain unconfirmed or unspecified. The response to an unacceptable approval is also unspecified.
The reviewer checks approvers and statuses in Concur, then screenshots them and saves the report PDF.
The reviewer flags receipt or personal-expense checks that do not meet the AEA rulebook to the submitter or client and records the resolution in the tracker.
Only cleared reports enter the scrubbing batch; reports with flagged issues remain out while resolution is pending.
The named AEA variant's differences from a common route and their basis have not been described.

The Excel review tracker is used by the reviewer to add an AEA Concur expense report at the start of review.
The Excel review tracker is used to log a report for review, with fields for cardholder, statement total, submitted amount, report identifier, and status.
The current AEA rulebook is the reported source for receipt adequacy and personal-expense classification; it has not been supplied for review.
The reviewer screenshots the Concur approvers and statuses and saves the report PDF as part of the review.
The review tracker records resolutions of flagged receipt or personal-expense issues.
The work is named Expense Processing: T&E Review & Scrubbing (AEA Variant).

The current AEA rulebook determines receipt adequacy and correct personal-expense classification.
The receipt threshold is not yet confirmed.
Only cleared reports go into the scrubbing batch.
The work reviews AEA Concur expense reports and logs them in an Excel review tracker.
